questions.text: Crystals of Bt toxin produced by some bacteria, do not kill the bacteria producing them because :
questions.solution:
The Bacillus thuringiensis bacterium produces the Bt toxin as an inactive protoxin in crystalline form.

The protoxin becomes active only in the alkaline gut of the insect, where it is solubilised and cleaved. Hence the toxin is harmless to the bacterium that makes it.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Biotechnology produces transgenic micro-organisms that act as microfactories for proteins.

Reason (R) : To produce proteins for human use like insulin, transgenic microorganisms can be developed.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: transgenic micro-organisms carrying a foreign gene act as microfactories producing useful proteins. It is true.

Reason: transgenic micro-organisms can be developed to make proteins such as insulin for human use. It is true.

The reason only gives one example of the proteins made and does not explain why biotechnology produces transgenic micro-organisms that act as microfactories, so it is not the correct explanation.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text: Which one of the following transgenic animals is being used to test the safety of the polio vaccine ?
questions.solution:
Transgenic mice are used to test the safety of the polio vaccine. This is used instead of monkeys, which were the earlier test animals, and it reduces the cost and the number of animals needed.

Sheep, goat and pig are not used for this test.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text: The improved trait that is found in the genetically modified transgenic crop – Golden rice is :
questions.solution:
Golden rice is a transgenic rice variety in which genes for the synthesis of β -carotene have been introduced. β -carotene is the precursor of vitamin A, so the improved trait is a high vitamin-A content. Insect resistance is the trait of Bt crops, and high lysine or protein content belongs to other biofortified varieties.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Indian Government has set up an organisation known as GEAC to decide the validity of GM research.

Reason (R) : Genetic modification of organisms has no effect when such organisms are introduced in the ecosystem.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The Government of India set up the Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee (GEAC) to decide the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services, so Assertion (A) is true. Genetic modification can have unpredictable effects on the ecosystem, which is why such regulation is needed, so Reason (R) is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: The specific Bt toxin genes which protect the cotton plants against the cotton bollworms are :
questions.solution:
Bt cotton carries the genes of Bacillus thuringiensis that code for insecticidal Cry proteins active against lepidopteran larvae.

The proteins encoded by cryIAc and cryIIAb control the cotton bollworms, whereas cryIAb controls the corn borer.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Functional ADA cDNA genes must be inserted in the lymphocytes at the early embryonic stage in gene therapy for ADA deficiency.

Reason (R) : Cells in the embryonic stage are immortal, differentiated and easy to manipulate.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
Assertion: in gene therapy for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes cultured from the patient receive the functional ADA cDNA, but these cells are short-lived, so the treatment must be repeated. For a permanent cure the gene must be introduced into cells at the early embryonic stage. The Assertion is true.

Reason: embryonic cells are totipotent and undifferentiated, and they are not immortal. The Reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: ELISA technique is based on the principle of
questions.solution:
ELISA (enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay) detects a pathogen through its antigens, or through the antibodies made against them, by means of antigen–antibody interaction. It is therefore based on antigen–antibody interaction.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Patents are granted by government to an inventor.

Reason (R) : Patents prevents others from commercial use of an invention.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
A patent is granted by the government to an inventor, so Assertion (A) is true.

A patent gives the inventor the exclusive right to make and sell the invention for a fixed period and prevents others from using it commercially without permission. Reason (R) is true and explains why the patent is granted.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : In molecular diagnosis, single stranded DNA or RNA tagged with radioactive molecule is called a probe.

Reason (R) : A probe always searches and hybridises with its complementary DNA in a clone of cells.
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
questions.solution:
A probe is a single-stranded DNA or RNA tagged with a radioactive molecule, so the assertion is true. The probe hybridises with its complementary DNA in a clone of cells, and the clone with the mutated gene shows up on autoradiography. This explains why the probe is used in molecular diagnosis, so the reason correctly explains the assertion.

Hence, the correct option is (A).

questions.text: Who among the following challenged the patent right granted to the University of Mississippi Medical Centre for ‘use of turmeric in wound healing’ ?
questions.solution:
The patent granted to the University of Mississippi Medical Centre for the use of turmeric in wound healing was challenged by the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), headed by Dr. R.A. Mashelkar. CSIR showed that the healing use of turmeric was already known in India for centuries, and the patent was revoked as biopiracy.

Hence, the correct option is (D).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : A patient of ADA deficiency undergoing treatment for gene therapy requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes.

Reason (R) : Lymphocytes are immortal.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
In gene therapy for ADA deficiency, lymphocytes from the patient's blood are grown in culture, a functional ADA cDNA is introduced into them using a retroviral vector, and the cells are returned to the patient. Since these lymphocytes are not immortal and have a limited life span, the patient needs periodic infusions of genetically engineered lymphocytes. Hence, the Assertion is true.

The Reason is false because lymphocytes are mortal; the cure becomes permanent only when the gene is introduced into marrow cells at an early embryonic stage.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following products was produced as a result of DNA manipulation in the first transgenic cow ‘Rosie’ ?
questions.solution:
The first transgenic cow, Rosie (1997), produced human protein-enriched milk containing the human α -lactalbumin, 2.4 grams per litre.

Hence, the correct option is (B).

questions.text:
Assertion (A) : Crystal protein Bt toxin does not kill the Bacillus but kills the insects.

Reason (R) : Bt toxin exists in inactive form in Bacillus but when ingested by the insect, the acidic pH of its gut changes it into an active form.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
questions.solution:
The Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in Bacillus, so the bacterium is not killed, hence the assertion is true. In the insect gut the alkaline (not acidic) pH solubilises the crystals and activates the toxin, so the reason is false.

Hence, the correct option is (C).

questions.text: Which one of the following is used during ‘RNA i’ process, to silence the desired gene ?
questions.solution:
RNA interference silences a gene post-transcriptionally. Double-stranded RNA (dsRNA) complementary to the mRNA of the target gene is introduced into the cell. It is processed into short fragments that bind and degrade the complementary mRNA, so the protein is not formed.

dsDNA, rDNA and DNA polymerase do not take part in this silencing.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
